summary: iter20 — Backend (14/14 pytest passed) and Frontend (full follow/unfollow flow + toasts + count delta verified) for the new follow + listing-publish-notify feature. All 14 backend cases green: follow-status (unauth/auth), POST/DELETE follow (401, 404, 403 frozen, increment, idempotent, decrement), listing_notify direct (sent + already_announced + not_published + product_not_found + maker_not_found), and end-to-end create-published / publish-draft endpoints both stamp published_at. Frontend on /makers/iron-and-oak: unauthed shows '+ Sign in to follow' (data-testid=follow-btn-follow), authed shows '+ Follow', click toggles to '✓ Following' with sonner toast 'Following Iron & Oak Studio. You'll get an email when they post.', count bumps 0→1; second click reverts to '+ Follow' with 'Unfollowed Iron & Oak Studio.' toast, count back to 0. Idempotency stamp + email-429 graceful handling confirmed by tests (first call sent:true, second already_announced).
critical_code_review_comments: listing_notify.py — clean idempotency design via published_at stamp; each send_* call wrapped in try/except so one transient mailer failure (e.g. MailerSend 429) doesn't fail the whole fan-out. Good.

routers/follows.py — uses upsert with $setOnInsert for idempotent follow; count_documents call is fine given expected scale (small follower lists per maker). For very-high-fan makers, consider denormalizing follower_count onto the maker doc + $inc on insert/delete.

Inconsistency: lib/api.js uses TWO different localStorage keys for buyers — community endpoints (showcase/forum/files) read 'cm_buyer_jwt' (buyerAuthHeaders) while FollowButton.jsx reads 'cm_community_jwt'. If users are minted via /community/auth/magic/verify, the frontend stores JWT under one key; the FollowButton would then never see it. Recommend consolidating to a single key (preferred 'cm_community_jwt' since that's what the new code uses, OR migrate FollowButton to 'cm_buyer_jwt' to match the rest). Note: for testing I seeded cm_community_jwt as the spec required, so this didn't surface in this iteration's manual flow — but real users going through magic-verify may hit a broken authed UX.

maker.py maker_create_product L317-329: notify is called inside the create endpoint synchronously. For a published listing with many followers, this can add latency. Consider FastAPI BackgroundTasks (already imported) to fan out asynchronously.

maker_publish_product does not check whether status was already 'published' before re-publishing — if a listing is already live, calling /publish again resets expires_at AND accrues another listing_publish charge. Idempotency only protects the email broadcast; the billing side may double-charge. (Existing behavior, not introduced this iter, but flagging for review.)
FollowButton.jsx: link to /makers/${makerSlug}#followers anchor goes nowhere (no #followers section rendered yet). Either remove the anchor or add a follower-list section.

listing_notify computes follower_count inside the cursor loop — if a follower doc lacks follower_email it's still counted toward follower_count but skipped for follower_sent. That's the correct semantic (matches the test) but worth documenting.
test_credentials: Buyer JWT minted via maker_auth.issue_session_jwt(uid,email,role='buyer') with prior community_users upsert (moderation_status='active').
seed_data_creation: All test data prefixed TEST_; community_users + follow rows + test products are cleaned up in pytest teardown and after the playwright run. No persistent data left.
context_for_next_testing_agent: iter20 covers: db.follows collection + follow-status/POST/DELETE endpoints, listing_notify.notify_listing_published idempotency via published_at stamp, maker_create_product + maker_publish_product hooks. The MailerSend 429 quota was hit during iter20 testing too — broadcast succeeds structurally (counts return correctly) but actual emails may not deliver. NOTE: there is a localStorage-key inconsistency between FollowButton (reads 'cm_community_jwt') and the rest of the buyer code (reads 'cm_buyer_jwt' via buyerAuthHeaders). Worth main-agent attention before the feature ships to real users — the ad-hoc test seeded the right key, but real magic-verify flow may store under the other key. test helpers at /tmp/mint_buyer.py + /tmp/cleanup_buyer.py.
